newsitem.title: JORDAN: Amman stock steady in mostly banks led demand.
newsitem.headline: Amman stock steady in mostly banks led demand.

text.p: Jordanian shares were steady at the start of weekly trade on Saturday in healthy trade mainly buttressed by orders on banks and industrials, dealers said.
The official 60-share Amman Financial Market (AFM) index shed 0.22 percent to 166.50 points on high turnover worth 2.08 million dinars ($2.9 million) dominated by a few block sales.

"The prices are steady but in an upward trend with demand mostly focused on banks in the first place and followed by industrials generated by local investors," said Ibrahim Odeh, a broker at Wataniyeh Financial Services.
But the volume was largely due to a large block trade in 300,000 shares worth 1.5 million dinars in Arab International Hotels which owns the five-star Amman Marriott.
Aside from this deal, rumoured to have been foreign inspired, the bourse saw primarily locally fuelled demand on some blue-chip industrials expected to post healthy half-year results, dealers said.
Arab Pharmaceutical Manufacturing rose 0.08 dinars to 4.16 82,130 dinars worth of trade in market expectations of healthy half year results.
Heavyweight Arab Bank, which drove the official index up to a three-year high earlier in July, shed 2.00 dinars to 294 in minimal trade, helping to drag the market lower.
Local investors piled into the shares in recent weeks, anticipating strong 1997 profits, announcements of a bonus share offering and government plans to scrap foreign share ownership ceilings.
Overall 12 shares rose on Saturday and 18 fell with a similar number trading but closing unchanged.

The private Pearl Index of the 45 best-performing shares in terms of turnover and financial performance, fixed at 100 points at the end of 1994, shed 0.24 percent to 80.97 points, 2.91 percent down since the start of the year. $1 = 0.709 dinars
